title: Unauthenticated tenant access through client X-Tenant-ID fallback
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-01/02 (HTTP 200 read of tenant-B data; HTTP 201 send as tenant B, no token)
expected_behaviour: 401 for any request without a verified bearer token; tenant only from token
actual_behaviour: Tenant taken from X-Tenant-ID header when no token is present
business_impact: Any internet caller can read/alter another tenant's notifications, workflows, DLQ, automation rules, voice sessions/transcripts
security_impact: Cross-tenant data disclosure and tampering (P0 launch blocker #1)
recommended_solution: Replace get_optional_security_context with get_security_context on all non-webhook routes; delete every 'ctx.tenant_id if ctx else x_tenant_id'; add a route-auth regression test that fails on any unauthenticated non-allowlisted route
verification_method: Re-run route audit (evidence/claude-inspection/static/route_auth_audit.json) + SEC-PROBE-01/02 expecting 401

title: Payment webhook HMAC secret is a source constant shared by all tenants
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-03 (forged payment_intent.succeeded -> order.payment_status=PAID)
expected_behaviour: Per-tenant provider secret from a secret store, timestamp tolerance, amount/currency match, provider reconciliation before PAID
actual_behaviour: Constant secret in Git, tenant from query string, no timestamp, no amount check
business_impact: Goods can be released for unpaid orders
recommended_solution: Load secret per tenant/integration from vault; verify provider signature scheme (e.g. Stripe t=,v1=); reject stale timestamps; compare amount/currency with intent; mark PAID only after provider API reconciliation
verification_method: Forged-signature, replay, wrong-amount and wrong-tenant webhook tests must fail

title: Refund approval: client-asserted MFA, no cumulative cap, no idempotency, self-approval
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-04 (3 x 100% refunds approved via 'X-MFA-Verified: true'; 300000 refunded vs 100000 captured)
expected_behaviour: Server-verified step-up MFA; sum(refunds) <= captured; unique idempotency key; approver != requester
actual_behaviour: MFA flag from header/query; per-refund check only vs order total; key ignored
business_impact: Direct financial loss
recommended_solution: Use context.mfa_verified (fresh step-up JWT claim) only; SELECT FOR UPDATE order + SUM existing refunds; UNIQUE(tenant_id, idempotency_key); forbid approved_by == requested_by; call provider refund API before COMPLETED
verification_method: Negative tests for header MFA, over-refund, duplicate key, self-approval

title: Quote approval MFA satisfied by any non-null mfa_code
observed_evidence: Static: mfa_verified=context.mfa_verified or (req.mfa_code is not None)
expected_behaviour: TOTP verified against the approver's enrolled, encrypted seed
actual_behaviour: Any string accepted
business_impact: Discounts/margins above policy can be approved without second factor
recommended_solution: Verify req.mfa_code with SecurityService.verify_totp against the user's seed (or require fresh mfa_verified token); add test with wrong code
verification_method: Approval with mfa_code='000000' (wrong) must return 403

title: Customer voice OTP backdoor '123456'
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-05 (unauthenticated caller verified with 123456, no OTP issued)
expected_behaviour: Verification only against a server-generated, delivered, single-use OTP
actual_behaviour: Static code always accepted
business_impact: Any caller hears another customer's orders/account data
recommended_solution: Delete the fallback; issue OTP via SMS/WhatsApp provider; persist OTP hash with TTL/attempts in PostgreSQL/Redis; update the test to request and use the issued OTP
verification_method: verify-caller with 123456 must return verified=false

title: Manager voice step-up accepts any 6/8-char string; action tokens not bound to tenant/user; 'executed' does nothing
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-06/07 ('abcdef' accepted; tenant-B manager consumed tenant-A token)
expected_behaviour: Cryptographic TOTP verification; token bound to tenant+user; real domain command executed through policy
actual_behaviour: Length check only; global in-memory dict; no domain call
business_impact: High-risk spoken actions approvable without MFA; UI reports false execution
recommended_solution: Verify TOTP with SecurityService.verify_totp; store previews in PostgreSQL with tenant_id/user_id/expiry and check them on consume; dispatch to the owning domain service; return executed only on domain success
verification_method: Wrong TOTP and foreign-tenant token must return 403

title: AI tool gateway returns hardcoded fixtures (no domain handlers registered)
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/security/runtime_security_probes.json SEC-PROBE-12 (orders.get_status('DOES-NOT-EXIST') -> PAID, tracking AMN-2026-88741)
expected_behaviour: Every tool calls the tenant-scoped domain service and returns fresh authoritative data
actual_behaviour: Constant dictionaries (stock 15, price 100000, PAID)
business_impact: Customers told false prices, stock and payment status
security_impact: Hallucinated financial claims presented as verified evidence (SAI-08, invariant 8)
recommended_solution: Register real handlers (CatalogService, InventoryService.atp, PricingService.calculate, OrderService.get) via tool_gateway.register_handler at app startup; make _execute_builtin_tool raise TOOL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; derive tool params from the router/LLM function-call, not keyword+hardcoded IDs
verification_method: Agent turn about a real order returns that order's DB status

title: OutputGuard fails open without evidence; price regex gaps

verification_method: Guard corpus incl. 'MAD 999', 'dirhams', no-evidence cases

title: RLS cannot be used by the running product: least-privileged role breaks login/webhooks; template uses superuser; code default is SQLite
files_lines: src/backend/core/config.py:23-26; .env.example (DATABASE_URL user postgres); src/backend/api/auth.py:40; api/quotes.py:235; api/payments.py:75
observed_evidence: evidence/claude-inspection/db/no_context_visibility.txt (app role sees 0 users/quotes/payment_intents without tenant ctx; superuser sees 57 users)
expected_behaviour: App runs as sales_app_user with RLS; pre-auth lookups use a narrowly-scoped SECURITY DEFINER function or a separate non-tenant table
actual_behaviour: Working config requires RLS bypass (superuser) or SQLite (no RLS)
business_impact: Either login does not work, or tenant isolation depends only on application WHERE clauses
security_impact: Tenant isolation not enforced in any functional deployment (launch blocker #1)
recommended_solution: Add SECURITY DEFINER lookup functions (login by email+tenant slug, webhook route lookup) owned by a dedicated role; switch DATABASE_URL to sales_app_user; remove SQLite default; add a startup check refusing superuser/BYPASSRLS connections
verification_method: Run full API test suite against sales_app_user; startup must fail when connected as superuser

title: Insecure default secrets with no production guard (JWT HS256, MFA key, webhook, telephony, webchat)

actual_behaviour: Defaults silently used when .env is absent
business_impact: Anyone with repo access can mint admin JWTs for any tenant on a mis-configured deployment
recommended_solution: Remove defaults (Field(...)), validate entropy at startup, move to Docker secrets/Vault; prefer OIDC/JWKS (RS256) as specified in Step 02
verification_method: Boot with no env must fail; secret scan in CI

title: Unauthenticated voice WebSocket and telephony inbound; optional signature; recording consent defaulted to true
